subject: PD
stem: 6-week-old persistent non-bilious vomiting, hungry, wants to feed, K+ 3.1, olive mass. Diagnosis?
explanation: Non-bilious projectile vomiting 3–8w + hungry + olive + hypochloraemic alkalosis = pyloric stenosis. US confirms; correct electrolytes then pyloromyotomy.

subject: PD
stem: Term neonate day 3: abdominal distension, delayed meconium day 3, no stool after, dilated loops on X-ray. Diagnosis?
explanation: Delayed meconium >48h + distension + dilated loops = Hirschsprung. Biopsy (aganglionosis); contrast enema transition zone.

subject: PD
stem: Mother A-negative, no anti-D last pregnancy, husband unknown. Term boy severe jaundice within hours. Most likely?
options: B. Rh haemolytic disease from alloimmunisation
explanation: Hours-after-birth severe jaundice + Rh-negative mother without prophylaxis = Rh HDN. Check DAT, bilirubin, Hb; phototherapy/exchange + IVIG per severity.

subject: PD
stem: Macrosomic infant of diabetic mother, glucose 3.2 mmol/L, vigorous. Management?
options: A. 10% dextrose IV bolus immediately in all
B. Encourage early breastfeeding + close glucose monitoring (≥2.5 threshold per recall protocol)
explanation: Asymptomatic 3.2 (>2.5) vigorous term: feed early + monitor. IV dextrose if <2.0–2.5, symptomatic, or persistent low.

subject: PD
stem: 3-day breastfed term: lethargic, poor feeding, new jaundice, T 35.4, liver 2 cm. Most likely?
explanation: Hypothermia + lethargy + poor feeding + jaundice = sepsis until proven otherwise. Cultures, antibiotics, glucose, bilirubin workup urgently.

subject: PD
stem: 18-month febrile seizure <5 min, generalised, quick recovery. Advice?
options: B. Reassure: simple febrile seizure usually benign; antipyretics, safety-net, no routine AED/EEG
explanation: Simple febrile seizure 6mo–5y: brief, generalised, once/24h, full recovery. Exclude meningitis by age/clues; educate, no chronic AED.

subject: PD
stem: 8-month winter wheeze, crackles, rhinorrhoea, RSV positive, mild distress. Best care?
options: B. Supportive: oxygen if needed, fluids, suction; no routine bronchodilator/steroid
C. Adult COPD inhaler high dose
explanation: Bronchiolitis is viral supportive care. Antibiotics/steroids not routine unless bacterial superinfection.

subject: PD
stem: 7-year-old recurrent wheeze responsive to salbutamol, atopy. Best controller?
options: A. Daily low-dose ICS ± LTRA; action plan + technique check
explanation: Childhood asthma: ICS backbone, step-up per control, spacer technique, trigger avoidance.

subject: PD
stem: 2-year-old watery diarrhoea, some dehydration, no blood. First therapy?
options: B. Low-osmolarity ORS + zinc + early feeding
explanation: Viral gastroenteritis: ORS is life-saving; zinc reduces duration; continue feeds; antibiotics only for cholera/shigella/amoeba per protocol.

subject: PD
stem: 5-year-old periorbital + leg oedema, heavy proteinuria, albumin low, cholesterol high. Diagnosis and first-line drug?
explanation: Nephrotic triad + hyperlipidaemia: minimal-change commonest; steroids first-line; monitor relapse, vaccinate, salt management.

subject: PD
stem: Girl iron-deficiency anaemia. Which parasite classically causes it?
explanation: Hookworm sucks blood → IDA. Fish tapeworm → B12 deficiency. Pinworm → perianal itch.

subject: PD
stem: Mode of inheritance of beta-thalassaemia major?
explanation: Beta-thal major needs two mutated HBB alleles – AR. Counselling + premarital screening crucial in region.

subject: PD
stem: Child with VP shunt since age 3 now febrile. Best temperature method + concern?
options: B. Avoid rectal thermometry; use axillary/tympanic/oral per age + evaluate shunt infection urgently
explanation: Fever + VP shunt = shunt infection until excluded. Use non-invasive thermometry; cultures, bloods, neurosurgery review – don't delay.

subject: PD
stem: 14-month boy born 8 weeks preterm: says baba/mama, walks unassisted, can't turn pages. Action?
options: B. Correct for gestational age + assess milestones – likely normal; reassure + surveillance
explanation: Correct age = 12 months: walking + 2 words is on track. Preterms need corrected-age assessment + hearing/vision screen + follow-up.

subject: PD
stem: 4-year-old fever, ear pain, rhinorrhoea, cervical nodes, mobile eardrum. Management if mild?
options: B. Symptomatic paracetamol + watchful waiting 48–72h; amoxicillin if severe/persistent (watchful-waiting criteria)
explanation: Mild AOM/viral URI with mobile drum: symptomatic first; antibiotics if bulging, otorrhoea, <2y bilateral, or no improvement.

subject: PD
stem: Parents of a child with diabetes insipidus ask what labs to expect. Which pattern fits DI?
options: A. High urine SG, low serum osmolality
B. Low urine SG, high serum osmolality + hypernatraemia + polyuria
explanation: DI: dilute polyuria → concentrated serum. Teach parents thirst, dehydration signs, desmopressin (central) vs thiazide/low salt (nephrogenic).

subject: PD
stem: A 12-month-old is due vaccines. When is MMR given?
options: B. First dose 12–15 months (second 4–6y); no need to repeat for endemic area if documented
explanation: MMR 12–15mo + 4–6y. Check UAE schedule; catch-up if missed; contraindicated in pregnancy/severe immunocompromise.

subject: PD
stem: Newborn hyperbilirubinaemia + anaemia + hypoproteinaemia day 1, O-negative mother antiglobulin positive, no antenatal care. Baby blood type likely?
options: B. Rh-positive (e.g. A+ or B+) – Rh-positive fetus in sensitised Rh-negative mother
explanation: Rh-positive fetus in sensitised Rh-negative mother → haemolysis. Type baby, DAT, bilirubin, treat aggressively to prevent kernicterus.
